title: Expatriates in Europe: Benny Bailey and rising nationalism
summary: They discuss players living in Europe, Griffin and Farmer, Benny Bailey planning to return, and French attitudes.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And you'll see some of those cats over there too, that would just simply be over there hanging out.
A lot of them are living over there.
That's what I mean. They'd just be living over there, hanging, just be trifling.
And when you become a resident of that country, you're a local boy. You are not getting one dime more than that other fellow.
That's right.

You see and it's hard and they think well we can work more over here. Doing what? What are you doing? They refuse to - when I ask them, I say what are you doing, man. You don't look like nothing you know. You don't look like me. My dungarees is cleaner than yours. You know what I mean. What you got? Show me. The only thing that the guys over there, you can count on one hand that's doing good. Johnny Griffi N, well he's got a house over there I understand in Holland somewhere, in Belgium somewhere where he lives with his family. Art Farmer lives in Vienna. He's got a house over there. Shit, man, that's about it.
Well, Benny Bailey, as long as Benny has been over there...
Benny Bailey told me that he's making a bee, he's going over to get his business straight and get his stuff and
he's coming back. He's through with it.

Essentially he told me the same thing. He told me he was feeling a wave of nationalism that's going on over there in Germany right now. And he said he wanted to get his hat before kinesis because he can feel it. They're getting funnier and funnier about the gigs over there.
I'm telling you man...
All them years he's been there and the reputation he's got in that country, if he's feeling it....
You better believe it, man.
And he's over there since 1947 or something around there.
That's right. He's been over there a long time. Most of his life.
Most of his life, that's right.

A long time. And I know in France, they don't care nothing about you man, in Paris. That's where you don't find no black jazz musicians in Paris. And they seem to be taking the music away from the French musicians.
Oh they're getting that attitude. If you're almost starting to play pretty good, so they get the attitude.
Yeah so they don't mess around the line of what you have done, man. So their attitude in Europe, they don't need you any more, you see.
That's right.
